items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: there was a focus appropriated the way Liszt did; Liszt showed the way, and it got to be very popular in the nineteenth century.

ctx.x: You brought that up, and I had forgotten about it, but that

was one of the most motivating things.
At that time you could have, as so many others did, go really into the classical sound. I never liked classic jazz, I always hated it. I still do. Whenever they have a jazz piece with a cast in a classical mold, done with a symphony orchestra, I say God, it's awful, in every case.
I always thought strongly in those days that this is not the way to do it, that you should make the music of the jazz people as valid as that music is, if you can, to use that form of expression,…
We're getting ahead of ourselves, but since you mentioned that, there's one question I've got to ask
